text.p: The Federal Communications Commission Thursday approved Westinghouse Electric Corp.'s $3.9 billion acquisition of Infinity Broadcasting Corp., which will strengthen Westinghouse's position as the nation's largest radio broadcaster.

The FCC said it approved waivers of rules on multiple ownership of media outlets in the same city and a request by Pittsburgh-based Westinghouse for permanent waivers to allow it to retain stations acquired in November 1995 from CBS Inc.
As a result of the merger, Westinghouse will acquire Infinity's 43 radio stations.

Westinghouse currently controls radio and television stations in nine markets where it will acquire Infinity radio stations -- New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Philadelphia, San Francisco, Detroit, Boston, Baltimore and Washington D.C.

In Boston, Baltimore and Washinton, Westinghouse controls permanent radio-television combinations. The FCC said it granted temporary one-to-a-market waivers in those markets for a period ending six months after the FCC issues its decision on television ownership.
Westinghouse announced plans to buy Infinity on June 20. Its shareholders approved an amendment on Dec. 10 to issue shares to complete the acquisition.
